text: Under 8 U.S.C. § 1401, a person born in the United States to parents who are subject to its jurisdiction is a citizen at birth. A child is born in California to two undocumented immigrant parents. Is the child a U.S. citizen at birth?

options.A: Yes, because birth in the United States generally confers citizenship.
options.B: No, because the parents are not lawful residents.

text: Under 8 U.S.C. § 1401(g), a person born abroad to one U.S. citizen parent and one alien parent is a citizen at birth if the citizen parent was physically present in the U.S. for at least five years, two of which were after age 14. A child is born abroad to a U.S. citizen mother who lived in the U.S. from age 5 to age 25. Is the child a citizen at birth?

options.A: Yes, because the mother meets the physical presence requirement.
options.B: No, because the child was born outside the United States.

text: Under 11 U.S.C. § 362, the filing of a bankruptcy petition operates as an automatic stay of most collection actions against the debtor. A creditor files a lawsuit to collect a debt on the day after the debtor files for Chapter 7 bankruptcy. Is the lawsuit stayed?

options.A: Yes, because the automatic stay applies immediately upon filing.
options.B: No, because the creditor filed before learning of the bankruptcy.

text: Under 11 U.S.C. § 727, the court shall grant the debtor a discharge in a Chapter 7 case unless the debtor committed certain frauds. A debtor intentionally concealed assets from the bankruptcy trustee. Should the court deny discharge?

options.A: Yes, because fraudulent concealment of assets is grounds for denial.
options.B: No, because the debtor still has the right to a fresh start.

text: Under the Statute of Frauds (Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 110), contracts for the sale of goods for $500 or more must be in writing. Alice orally agrees to sell Bob a used car for $3,000. Is the contract enforceable?

options.A: Yes, because Bob and Alice mutually agreed.
options.B: No, because a contract for the sale of goods over $500 must be in writing.

text: Under U.C.C. § 2-207, additional terms in an acceptance are proposals for addition to the contract between merchants. A seller sends a firm offer; the buyer accepts with a term requiring arbitration. Is the arbitration term automatically part of the contract?

options.A: Yes, because it was included in the buyer's acceptance.
options.B: No, because additional terms in an acceptance are proposals, not automatically binding.

text: Under U.C.C. § 9-322, a perfected security interest has priority over an unperfected security interest. Bank A perfects its security interest in a debtor's equipment. Bank B later obtains an unperfected security interest in the same equipment. Which bank has priority?

options.A: Bank A, because it perfected first.
options.B: Bank B, because its interest arose later.

text: Under the doctrine of res ipsa loquitur, a plaintiff may rely on the circumstances of an accident to infer negligence when the accident is of a kind that ordinarily does not occur in the absence of negligence. A patient wakes up from surgery with a surgical sponge left inside. May res ipsa apply?

options.A: Yes, because sponges do not remain inside patients absent negligence.
options.B: No, because the plaintiff cannot identify the specific negligent act.
